ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the large rectangle is divided by black lines into six squares: one largest square at the upper left; two equal bottom-row squares at the lower left and lower middle; one smallest small square near the right in the middle; one square at the upper right; and one square at the lower right. It is known that the side length of the smallest square is 1. Reasoning: Let the side length of the two equal bottom-row squares at the lower left and lower middle be x, and the side length of the largest square at the upper left be L. From the width relationship in the figure, the side length of the upper-left large square equals the sum of the widths of the two bottom-row squares minus the 1 of the small square, that is, L = 2x - 1. Then look at the relationship between the right side and the middle notch: the upper-left large square is 1 taller than the upper-right square, the upper-right square is 1 wider than the lower-right square, and the lower-right square is 1 taller than the bottom-row square, so L = x + 3. Combining 2x - 1 = x + 3 gives x = 4, therefore L = 2(4) - 1 = 7.
